title: Add RAG Chronicle: storyboarding templates and deterministic playback runner
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: authors repeatedly requested a reproducible authoring flow for complex RAG scenarios that can be inspected, time-traveled, and replayed against different model variants. This PR introduces the 'RAG Chronicle' quickstart: a lightweight storyboarding template format and a deterministic playback runner for local and CI replay.

What this delivers: a compact storyboard YAML format for defining stepwise user interactions, index snapshots, tool-call stubs and telemetry checkpoints; a TypeScript playback runner that rehydrates KV caches and simulates streaming tokens to reproduce recorded runs; a docs quickstart with guided walk-through and troubleshooting notes; and an e2e replay test that validates deterministic outputs for a seeded demo session.

Key design notes: Chronicle is intentionally storage-agnostic (JSON/YAML snapshots) and focuses on deterministic replay for developer debugging and evals rather than production diagnostics. The playback runner includes options to snapshot and restore prefix caches, mock external tool endpoints, and inject synthetic latency to exercise timeouts. The format supports optional assertions per step to enable CI-level regression checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Add storyboard schema and example templates
- [x] Implement playback runner with cache rehydration and tool-mock harness
- [x] Add docs/quickstart with developer walkthrough and examples
- [x] Add CI e2e that runs a seeded demo session and asserts token-level diffs
- [x] Smoke test on macOS and in the Linux CI runner

Backward compatibility: This lives under quickstarts and does not change API surface of core SDKs. The runner depends on the dev SDK helpers in quickstarts; changes are limited to the new folder.

Usage example (excerpt): storyboard.yaml content is included in the quickstart README; basic run: yarn workspace @redwood/quickstarts rag-chronicle:replay --session examples/demo-session.json --assertions.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the deterministic seed handling, the mock tool adapter contract (simple HTTP stub interface) and the CI assertion hooks. I left a couple of TODOs for optional CLI flags (dry-run vs record) that we can follow up in a smaller change.

chore: update package.json workspace scripts for rag-chronicle
review_comments: Aisha Roy: Nice work — the storyboard YAML is compact. Two nits: rename 'kv_snapshot' to 'kv_cache' for clarity and add a short paragraph about size limits. Also please add one inline example of a tool stub response payload.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed both in latest commit; renamed field and added example payload in tool-mock.ts and README.
Carlos Mendes: Playback runner looks solid. One security note: tool-mock exposes an HTTP port by default; can we scope it to loopback only and document the flag?
Maya Patel (author): Updated tool-mock to bind 127.0.0.1 by default and documented --host flag in README.
Donovan Lee: e2e is useful. For CI resilience, recommend a retry-on-flaky-network wrapper for the replay test; not necessary to block merge.
Maya Patel (author): Added a small retry wrapper in the e2e harness and noted it in CI comments; ponged infra for flaky runners.
release_notes: Add 'RAG Chronicle' quickstart: storyboarding templates, deterministic playback runner, example sessions, and CI replay tests to help developers reproduce and debug RAG workflows locally.
